$comment: The predefined runs of ./rr report: per scenario, per emitter, the sizes, seeds and options. A list in options measures every value as its own variant. Sizes and seeds live only here, per framework.

$bench.$comment: ./rr bench: one app per framework, at the largest size every framework builds in every scenario (beni-direct has no 128 or 256 in unique-components).

beni-direct.$comment: No 256: beni's ownership checker (its 64-path width cap) refuses the N=256 app on browser-direct, every seed; see frameworks/beni-direct/README.md.

No 32, 128 or 256: beni's ownership checker (its 64-path width cap; every widget adds list paths to the one update summary) refuses the app with LIST MAY BE SHARED: N=32 for seed 3, N=96, 128 and 256 for every seed tried; see frameworks/beni-direct/README.md and notes/2026-10-16-beni-unique-components.md.

big-component.$comment: No digest: on the flat form it fails the prototype locality rule (calls per local action grow 8.6x from N=16 to 256, 14x from 64 to 1024), so it is excluded until fixed; see frameworks/digest/README.md (big-component) and notes/2026-10-16-big-component-digest-flat.md.

also.digest: fails the locality rule here (calls per local event grow 8.6x from N=16 to 256); timed for reference only

$bench.$comment: N=1 only: the js-framework-benchmark app, the calibration point (scenarios/big-table/README.md); growth with N is left to ./rr work.

beni-tea.$comment: Only N=1: from N=2 (seed 2) up, tables whose selection marker is aria-selected replace the selected <tr> instead of updating it, because beni cannot remove an aria-* attribute and refuses an optional one; that fails the node-identity rule, so those sizes do not count. N=1 (table 1 is js-framework-benchmark, marked by class) passes and is kept for the CPU bench. See notes/2026-10-16-beni-big-table.md.

beni-direct.$comment: Only N=1: from N=2 (seed 2) up, tables whose selection marker is aria-selected replace the selected <tr> instead of updating it, because beni cannot remove an aria-* attribute and refuses an optional one; that fails the node-identity rule, so those sizes do not count. N=1 (table 1 is js-framework-benchmark, marked by class) passes and is kept for the CPU bench. See notes/2026-10-16-beni-big-table.md. Its ownership checker also refuses N=16 and up.
